review_notes: I read the whole file and the Mathlib TopAdj simp lemmas for toSSetObjEquiv (naturality, δ and σ are simp). I also checked downstream uses in SphereTopologyTest/SingularTransfer.lean and SphereTopologyTest/SingularLifts.lean. The continuous-map simp lemmas (_apply, _symm_apply_apply, _symm_apply_comp) have clear normal forms and no cycles, and I found no problem with them. I could not run Lean, so both findings are judgments from reading the simp sets. They are not observed simp failures.

findings.excerpt:
X.toSSetObjEquiv k ((toSSet.map p).app k u) =
      p.hom.comp (Y.toSSetObjEquiv k u) :=
  rfl
findings.problem: This is the canonical bridge from singular-simplex maps back to continuous-map composition. It is not tagged `@[simp]`. Mathlib's neighbouring `toSSetObjEquiv_naturality_apply`, `_δ_apply` and `_σ_apply` are all simp, so `toSSetObjEquiv` of an operator application normalises automatically. `toSSetObjEquiv` of a `toSSet.map p` application does not. Callers must `rw` or `.trans` it by hand. The file does this in `singularLiftEquiv` (lines 204 and 207) and in `bijective_singularLiftRestrict` (line 266). A downstream test does `rw [TopCat.toSSetObjEquiv_map]` and only then calls `simp [...]`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `toSSetObjEquiv_map`. The LHS head is `toSSetObjEquiv _ (_.app _ _)` and the RHS is `p.hom.comp (...)`. The RHS contains no `toSSet.map` application, so it cannot loop. Since it is `rfl`, a `dsimp`-style simp lemma would also work. Then drop the manual `rw [TopCat.toSSetObjEquiv_map]` in `SphereTopologyTest/SingularTransfer.lean` and the manual rewrites in the calc blocks here.
findings.benefit: Evaluation goals about lifted singular simplices would normalise to `C(·,·)` composition in one `simp` call, in line with how Mathlib already treats the other `toSSetObjEquiv` lemmas. Users would no longer need the separate manual rewrite step.

findings.problem: The simp lemma is redundant. `singularLiftRestrict_val` is already simp and rewrites `(singularLiftRestrict p α s u).val` to `(toSSet.obj Y).map α u.val`. The standard functor identity simp lemmas then reduce this for `α = 𝟙 k`. The file's own proof is just `by simp`, which shows the existing simp set already proves the statement. A second simp rule on the same head competes with `singularLiftRestrict_val` for no benefit. It adds a lemma to maintain, and a reader may think the identity case needs special treatment. The sibling `singularLiftRestrict_comp_val` is correctly left non-simp.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]` from `singularLiftRestrict_id_val`, or delete the lemma. Either way `singularLiftRestrict_val` plus the functor simp lemmas keep the same normal form.
findings.benefit: The simp set has one rule for restriction, `singularLiftRestrict_val`, and its output is the canonical form. This avoids overlapping rewrites and treats id and comp consistently.
